title: review-result verdict block
description:
The JSON payload embedded in a fenced ```review-result``` block inside a reviewer's PR comment (clagentic_loadout.merge.verdict). Single source of truth for the field set shared by the emit side (build_verdict_block) and the gate-consumer side (parse_verdict_block, read_reviewer_verdict — the merge gate's verdict-fence assertion). Field set is deliberately minimal: reviewer identity, outcome, the SHA the reviewer evaluated, the PR number, and (optional) the model the reviewer self-reports having run as plus, from fence_schema_version 2, the findings state (open findings, cleared claims, scanner outcomes). A fence without a version is version 1 and stays valid.

NOTE on head_sha: this schema intentionally does NOT declare a format pattern on head_sha. read_reviewer_verdict() performs a dedicated full-40-char clagentic_loadout.sha.validate_sha(allow_abbreviated=False) check AFTER parse_verdict_block() returns, raising a specific 'malformed head_sha stamp' error distinct from a generic schema violation. Adding a head_sha pattern at the schema layer would upstage that dedicated check and its distinct error message.

NOTE on model_attested: this field is CALLER-SUPPLIED FREE TEXT, exactly like 'reviewer' — this schema does not, and cannot, verify it names the model that actually produced the review. See clagentic_loadout.merge.model_attestation's module docstring for why no tool-witnessed alternative exists at this seam today, and what enforcement this field's downstream check does and does not provide.

reviewer.description: Name/role that produced this verdict. Not constrained to any enum here: the value is the reviewer's own self-reported name and is authenticated independently by comment authorship (user.login), not by this field.

head_sha.description: Hex git SHA the reviewer evaluated, hand-carried for the SHA-stamp freshness check. Shape (full 40-char lowercase hex) is validated downstream, not by this schema.

pr_number.description: PR number the verdict applies to.

model_attested.description: OPTIONAL, caller-supplied free text naming the model backend the reviewer reports having run as (e.g. a resolved model identifier, not a bare tier alias). This is a SELF-REPORTED claim, not a tool-witnessed fact — see clagentic_loadout.merge.model_attestation for the shape/denylist check applied downstream and its documented trust limits.

fence_schema_version.description: OPTIONAL fence schema version. Absent means 1. Version 2 marks a fence that carries findings state (findings_open, supersedes, cleared_claims, scanners_run). Version 3 marks a fence that also carries the computed verdict (verdict_outcome, verdict_reasons, evaluator_version, policy_base_sha, evaluated_findings). Version 4 marks a fence from a review that ran against a sealed spec, carrying spec_hash, spec_tags and spec_coverage; it is a superset of version 3 and adds nothing to the computed verdict. A version 1 fence stays valid and reads as asserting no open findings; a fence below version 3 reads as not evaluated.

verdict_outcome.description: OPTIONAL, version 3. The verdict the evaluator computed from the findings, the stakes and the policy at the base revision. Computed by the tool, never typed by the reviewer. Absent means the fence was not evaluated.

verdict_reasons.description: OPTIONAL, version 3. One line for each reason the outcome is not CLEAN: a stale head, a degraded input, a blocking finding. Empty for CLEAN.

evaluator_version.description: OPTIONAL, version 3. Identifies the rules the verdict was computed under.

policy_base_sha.description: OPTIONAL, version 3. The base revision the policy (dispositions and stakes) was read from. Omitted when the base revision was not known.

evaluated_findings.description: OPTIONAL, version 3. The findings the outcome was computed from, each with the facts the reviewer stated about it. The merge gate computes the outcome again from these, under the policy it reads itself, so a fence that omits them cannot be re-checked.

file.description: Path the finding was raised on.

line.description: Line the finding was raised on.

rule_id.description: Rule the finding was raised under.

facts.description: The facts the reviewer stated, exactly as stated; judged against the published review-facts vocabulary, and anything outside it counts at its worst case.

severity.description: Present only for a finding that is not a defect and is not scored.

fingerprint.description: OPTIONAL link hint for the finding. Present only when the deployment records per-PR rulings, which are matched by it; absent otherwise.

findings_open.description: Findings the reviewer holds open at this verdict. A finding listed here and absent from a later fence's cleared_claims keeps the merge gate refusing.

id.description: Stable finding identifier, reused across fences.

rule_id.description: The rule the finding was raised under.

head.description: Head SHA the finding was raised at.

supersedes.description: Comment id of the earlier verdict comment this one replaces. Provenance only: replacing a comment does not clear the findings it held open.

cleared_claims.description: Findings the reviewer resolved at the head this verdict is for, each with one line of evidence.

id.description: Identifier of the finding that was cleared.

head.description: Head SHA the finding was cleared at; must equal this verdict's head_sha to count.

evidence.description: One line stating why the finding no longer applies.

scanners_run.description: Per scanner, whether it ran. A clean verdict is only as strong as the scanners behind it. Each scanner name must appear at most once; a verdict that lists the same scanner twice is rejected.

reason.description: Why the scanner did not run or failed. Required for every status but ran.

failure_sequences.description: OPTIONAL evidence. For each blocking finding that stated one, the concrete steps that trigger the defect and the damage that results. Informational: it holds no finding open and clears none.

file.description: Path of the finding the sequence belongs to.

rule_id.description: Rule the finding was raised under.

failure_sequence.description: The trigger steps and the resulting damage.

dropped.description: OPTIONAL evidence. Candidate findings the reviewer examined and dropped, each with the reason. Informational: a dropped candidate is not a finding.

file.description: Path the candidate was raised on.

line.description: Line the candidate was raised on.

rule_id.description: Rule the candidate was raised under.

resolved.description: OPTIONAL evidence. Prior findings a delta review closed this round, each at its prior location: resolved by the reviewer after re-judging it against the new head, or ruled resolved by the caller. Informational: a resolved finding is not open and is not re-posted.

file.description: Path the finding was raised on.

line.description: Prior location: the line in the numbering of the head the finding was raised against.

rule_id.description: Rule the finding was raised under.

reason.description: The caller's one-line reason. Required when by is caller.

fingerprint.description: The finding's fingerprint, when it had one.

spec_hash.description: OPTIONAL evidence, version 4. The sha256 of the sealed spec the review ran against. Present together with spec_tags and spec_coverage or not at all.

spec_tags.description: OPTIONAL evidence, version 4. The tag of each finding the review states: exactly one of in-spec, out-of-spec or fix-caused. Informational: a tag holds no finding open and clears none.

file.description: Path of the finding the tag belongs to.

rule_id.description: Rule the finding was raised under.

spec_tag.description: Whether the finding is within the spec's scope, outside it, or caused by a fix made during the build.

spec_coverage.description: OPTIONAL evidence, version 4. Each acceptance criterion of the sealed spec, once, as met or unmet.

criterion.description: The acceptance criterion id in the sealed spec.

status.description: Whether the change meets the criterion.

range.description: OPTIONAL evidence. The commit range the review covered: base..head for a full review, or since a previously reviewed head for a delta review.

basis.description: Which kind of range this is.

since.description: Previously reviewed head SHA, for basis since.

head.description: Head SHA the range ends at.

engines.description: OPTIONAL evidence. Which engine answered the run's chunks: the configured carrier, or the fallback that took over, with the model it ran as and why the carrier was not used.

model.description: Model label the profile declares for that engine.

reason.description: Why the carrier was not used, for a fallback.

chunks.description: How many chunks this engine answered.
